molecule.hpp — Molecular Data Structures

On this page

  • Overview

  • Constants

  • Utility Functions

  • Data Structures

Overview

Defines the core chemistry data types: the atomic coordinates, the molecular system (charge, multiplicity, atoms), and several helper functions for element lookup and physical constants.

Source file: include/molecule.hpp

Constants

ANG2BOHR

Conversion factor from Ångströms to Bohr radii.

inline constexpr double ANG2BOHR = 1.8897259886;

All atomic coordinates stored internally are in Bohr. Coordinates read from the TOML input file (assumed Ångströms) are multiplied by this constant immediately on parse.

Utility Functions

int atomic_number(const std::string &sym)
Parameters:

sym – Chemical symbol string (case-sensitive), e.g. "O", "Fe".

Returns:

Atomic number \(Z\).

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If the symbol is not found in the look-up table.

Returns the atomic number for a given element symbol. Covers H (1) through Xe (54).

int z = atomic_number("C");  // z == 6
std::string atomic_symbol(int Z)
Parameters:

Z – Atomic number 1–54.

Returns:

Element symbol string.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If Z is out of the supported range.

Inverse of atomic_number().

std::string sym = atomic_symbol(8);  // sym == "O"

Data Structures

struct Atom

Represents a single nucleus.

std::string symbol

Element symbol, e.g. "H".

int Z

Atomic number.

std::array<double, 3> coords

Cartesian coordinates (in Bohr).

struct Molecule

A complete molecular system.

std::vector<Atom> atoms

Ordered list of atoms.

int charge

Net molecular charge (default 0).

int multiplicity

Spin multiplicity \(2S+1\) (default 1). 1 → singlet (RHF eligible); 2 → doublet (UHF), etc.

int n_electrons() const

Returns \(\sum_A Z_A - \text{charge}\).

int n_alpha() const

Number of \(\alpha\)-spin electrons: \((N_e + (M-1))/2\) where \(M = \text{multiplicity}\).

int n_beta() const

Number of \(\beta\)-spin electrons: \(N_e - N_\alpha\).

double nuclear_repulsion() const

Nuclear repulsion energy in Hartree:

\[E_\text{nuc} = \sum_{A < B} \frac{Z_A Z_B}{R_{AB}}.\]
